why: Every number published between the published-bench markers of the documents listed under 'documents', held as data so tools/check_published_benchmarks.py can detect drift in either direction. Each figure names the document it is published in and cites a source, and each source states the provenance its kind requires: a measurement names its host, build flags, command, sampling, aggregation and runs (AGENTS.md section 8 item 7, INVARIANT-53).

ci-four-run-2026-09-20.description: The four benchmark-regression jobs per runner class that the README table reduces to a median and a min-max span. Per-run figures are in docs/BENCHMARK_HISTORY.md (2026-09-22, four-run re-base section) and in the 2026-09-22 entries of benchmarks/baseline.json and benchmarks/arm-baseline.json metadata.baseline_change_log. The derived percentages the region prints (the fast-class run's margin over the other three, the aarch64 spreads, the medians against their floors) are computed from those per-run figures. The wiki's per-algorithm pages (wiki/Cryptography-Algorithms.md and wiki/Post-Quantum-Cryptography.md) restate the ama_sha3_256_hash, ed25519_* and dilithium_* medians of that table and cite this source for them; they carry no figure the README table does not.
ci-four-run-2026-09-20.host: GitHub-hosted runners: ubuntu-latest (x86_64, a two-class fleet) and ubuntu-24.04-arm (aarch64), the benchmark-regression job of .github/workflows/ci.yml
ci-four-run-2026-09-20.build: cmake -B build -DAMA_USE_NATIVE_PQC=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DAMA_BUILD_TESTS=OFF -DAMA_BUILD_EXAMPLES=OFF -DAMA_ENABLE_AVX512=ON -DAMA_ENABLE_NATIVE_ARCH=ON; Python 3.11; pip install Cython>=3.0.0 and -e .[dev], so the six Cython bindings are built and imported
ci-four-run-2026-09-20.command: taskset -c 0 python benchmarks/benchmark_runner.py --verbose --baseline <benchmarks/baseline.json | benchmarks/arm-baseline.json> --require-runner-class <x86_64 | aarch64> --require-populated-baseline --output benchmarks/benchmark-results.json --markdown benchmark-report.md
ci-four-run-2026-09-20.sampling: benchmark_runner.py at heads ebc80b9, 1bf806b, da8901d and 1e79cd1: batches grown until a timed batch spans >= 0.15 s of wall-clock, 3 full-window batches per call; each job reports its fastest observation per row
ci-four-run-2026-09-20.aggregation: median of the four jobs per runner class (even count: mean of the middle two, rounded half up, computed by script from the job logs); min-max over the same four

ci-four-run-2026-09-07.description: The superseded Ed25519 four-run medians the region quotes for comparison (x86_64 / aarch64). Per-run figures are in the 2026-09-07 entries of benchmarks/baseline.json and benchmarks/arm-baseline.json metadata.baseline_change_log and in docs/BENCHMARK_HISTORY.md.
ci-four-run-2026-09-07.host: GitHub-hosted runners ubuntu-latest (x86_64) and ubuntu-24.04-arm (aarch64), the benchmark-regression job of .github/workflows/ci.yml
ci-four-run-2026-09-07.build: cmake -B build -DAMA_USE_NATIVE_PQC=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DAMA_BUILD_TESTS=OFF -DAMA_BUILD_EXAMPLES=OFF -DAMA_ENABLE_AVX512=ON -DAMA_ENABLE_NATIVE_ARCH=ON; Python 3.11; Cython bindings built
ci-four-run-2026-09-07.command: taskset -c 0 python benchmarks/benchmark_runner.py --verbose --baseline <per-architecture ledger> --require-runner-class <arch> --require-populated-baseline --output benchmarks/benchmark-results.json --markdown benchmark-report.md
ci-four-run-2026-09-07.sampling: benchmark_runner.py at heads f2ac1d8, 4a45408, 755cd22 and 447cdf0: batches grown until a timed batch spans >= 0.15 s, 3 full-window batches per call; fastest observation per row
ci-four-run-2026-09-07.aggregation: median of four jobs per runner class, even count: mean of the middle two, rounded half up

ci-single-run-2026-09-16.description: The single aarch64 run the 2026-09-16 floors for ed25519_keygen, ed25519_sign and full_package_verify were set from; the four 2026-09-20/21 runs confirm them. Recorded in the 2026-09-16 entry of benchmarks/arm-baseline.json metadata.baseline_change_log.

ci-single-run-2026-09-16.sampling: benchmark_runner.py at head 84ad90d2: batches grown until a timed batch spans >= 0.15 s, 3 full-window batches per call
ci-single-run-2026-09-16.aggregation: one run; fastest observation per row

regression-floor-ledger.description: Numbers read from the committed floor ledgers rather than measured by a run: the tolerances (45% on every x86_64 row; 15% on aarch64, 25% for full_package_create and dilithium_sign), the date the floors were last re-based, the host-independent ed25519_sign derivation (70,496 / 1.8469 = 38,170), the release the pre-discounting convention ended in, the 2026-09 audit the medians predate, and the date of the secp256k1 comb entry in the benchmark history.
regression-floor-ledger.reference: benchmarks/baseline.json and benchmarks/arm-baseline.json (tolerance_percent, metadata.baseline_change_log entries 2026-09-16 and 2026-09-22); docs/BENCHMARK_HISTORY.md section '2026-07-29: secp256k1 fixed-base comb'

specification.description: Document numbers of the standards a row or note cites: FIPS 202, FIPS 140-3, RFC 6979, RFC 8032.
specification.reference: the cited NIST FIPS and IETF RFC documents

source-constant.description: Counts fixed by this repository's code: the 1 KB message of the hash, MAC and AEAD rows and the 3 keys of hkdf_derive (one 96-byte native_hkdf output, three 32-byte keys) in benchmarks/benchmark_runner.py; the 4096 vectors of tests/c/test_x25519_fe64_mulx_equiv.c (N_VECTORS) and the 1024 of tests/c/test_x25519_field_equiv.c; the AMA_DISPATCH_USE_X25519_AVX2=1 opt-in value (src/c/dispatch/ama_dispatch.c); the secp256k1 comb's 16 entries (SECP256K1_COMB_SIZE), its ~1.9 KB size (16 x 3 x 5 limbs x 8 bytes = 1,920 bytes), and 64 doublings and additions (SECP256K1_COMB_BITS) against the ladder's 256 of each (src/c/ama_secp256k1.c).
